# RestMeta.LIST_DEFAULT_FILTERS is dead — declared on 11 models, never read by on_rest_list()

- **Kind**: bug
- **Date**: 2026-07-25
- **Requested by**: Ian (surfaced from a maestro-side notification-bell bug)

## Description

`RestMeta.LIST_DEFAULT_FILTERS` is documented as a supported property and
declared on 11 models across `account/` and `phonehub/`, but nothing in the
list query path ever reads it. Every list endpoint on those models returns
unfiltered rows. The property is inert.

Make it work, with an explicit precedence rule: the declared filter is a
**baseline** that an explicit same-field request param replaces, plus a global
off-switch for admin surfaces that need to see everything.

## Context

Confirmed downstream: the maestro notification bell called
`/api/account/notification` expecting only unread rows (the model declares
`{"is_unread": True}`) and got read + unread, so "mark all read" appeared
broken. Maestro was patched client-side (commit `c2a82a8` now passes
`?is_unread=true` explicitly) — that patch stays valid either way and needs no
revert. But the framework property is still dead for every other caller
relying on it, and `README.md:54` advertises it in the headline "define a
model" example.

`git log -S LIST_DEFAULT_FILTERS -- mojo/models/` returns nothing: the
consumer was never written, not removed.

**Decisions already made** (Ian, 2026-07-25):

1. **Rollout — engine + audit each declaration.** Make the property work, then
   review all 11 declarations and delete the ones that would hide rows an
   operator needs to see. `User.is_active` and `Group.is_active` are the prime
   suspects — activating them would hide deactivated users/tenants from admin
   lists. Do not assume the declarations are intentional; several were almost
   certainly written against an assumed behavior nobody ever exercised.
2. **Override semantics — same-name param replaces, plus a global off-switch.**
   `?is_unread=false` replaces the default for that field. Plus a framework
   param (e.g. `?_no_defaults=1`) that drops **all** default filters for the
   request. No magic `"all"` sentinel value — it would collide with fields that
   can legitimately hold the string `all`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `on_rest_list()` applies `get_rest_meta_prop("LIST_DEFAULT_FILTERS", {})`
      to the queryset.
- [ ] A default filter is **suppressed for its whole field** when the request
      names that field — including operator forms: `?is_unread=false`,
      `?is_unread__not=true`, `?is_unread__in=true,false`,
      `?is_unread__isnull=true`, and dotted relation keys (`?user.id=…` →
      `user__id`). Matching is on the **base field name** (`key_parts[0]` after
      `.`→`__`), not the literal key, and must consider exclusion filters too —
      `__not` / `__not_in` land in `excludes`, not `filters`.
- [ ] The global off-switch drops every default filter for that request.
- [ ] Defaults compose (AND) with the permission-scoped querysets
      `on_rest_handle_list()` passes into `on_rest_list()` — the owner-scoped
      and group-with-permission querysets are narrowing intersections, so a
      default filter layered on top is correct and must not be skipped just
      because a queryset was supplied.
- [ ] Defaults also apply to group scoping and to the aggregation path
      (`_mode` → `on_rest_list_aggregate`) — a count must match the list it
      describes.
- [ ] Detail-by-pk (`GET /api/x/<pk>`) is **unaffected** — defaults are a list
      concern only. `DM-025` relies on this (admins reaching an inactive group
      by pk).
- [ ] Each of the 11 declarations audited; risky ones removed with a one-line
      rationale in the commit message.
- [ ] Regression test: fails on current code (default not applied), passes on
      the fix. Cover baseline applied / same-field param replaces / exclusion
      form replaces / off-switch clears / composes with a perm-scoped queryset.
- [ ] Docs updated in both tracks + `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Investigation

- **What exists**:
  - Consumer: **none**. `mojo/models/rest.py:801` `on_rest_list()` builds from
    `cls.objects.all()` (or the passed-in queryset), applies group scoping
    (`:816-825`), then `on_rest_list_filter` (`:1119`, request params only),
    date-range (`:910`), sort (`:1252`), response (`:836`). No read of the
    property anywhere in `mojo/`.
  - `mojo/models/rest.py:569` `on_rest_handle_list()` is the only caller that
    passes a queryset — owner-scoped (`:593`) or group-with-permission
    (`:605`).
  - `mojo/models/rest.py:~1010-1116` `build_rest_filters()` is where request
    keys are parsed into `(filters, excludes)`; it already normalizes `.`→`__`,
    splits operator suffixes, and **skips every `_`-prefixed key as
    framework-reserved** (`:1032`) — so a `_no_defaults` param needs no new
    reserved-key handling. This function is the natural place to source the set
    of request-named fields for suppression, rather than re-parsing
    `QUERY_PARAMS` in `on_rest_list()`.

## Plan

### Objective

`RestMeta.LIST_DEFAULT_FILTERS` becomes a real, tested baseline filter on the
list query path: applied when declared, suppressed per-field by any request
param naming that field, and dropped wholesale by `?_no_defaults=1`. Ten of
the eleven existing declarations are deleted (the audit below shows each one
sits on the management surface for the very flag it would hide, or filters a
flag no code ever sets); `account.Notification` keeps its `{"is_unread": True}`
and becomes the engine's live proof.

### Scoping-phase findings that change the shape of the work

Three discoveries during exploration matter more than the original write-up
assumed:

1. **`build_rest_filters()` must not change signature.** It has three callers
   beyond the list path — `rest_aggregation._parse_stats_bundles()`
   (`mojo/models/rest_aggregation.py:185`) and two synthetic-request builders
   in `mojo/apps/assistant/services/tools/`. Adding a third return value would
   break them. The plan instead derives the request-named field set from the
   `(filters, excludes)` dicts it *already* returns — which is strictly more
   correct than re-parsing raw params, because every skip rule (reserved keys,
   `_`-prefixed keys, `sort`/`graph`/`search`, non-field names) has already
   been applied, and the partial-date expansion (`?created=2026-04` →
   `created__gte`/`created__lte`) and `__not_in`→`__in` rewrite both preserve
   the base field name.
2. **`push/delivery`'s declaration is provably wrong, not merely risky.**
   `NotificationDelivery.mark_delivered()` sets `status="delivered"` and
   `mark_failed()` sets `status="failed"` (`push/delivery.py:78-93`). A default
   of `{"status": "sent"}` would hide *successfully delivered* rows as well as
   failures. Nothing that was ever exercised would ship this.
3. **Three of the flags are never written `False` anywhere in `mojo/`** —
   `Passkey.is_enabled`, `GroupMember.is_active`, `RegisteredDevice.is_active`
   (repo-wide grep; the only `is_enabled` writers are `incident.IPSet`, an
   unrelated model). Those defaults are no-ops today and latent traps the day
   someone adds a disable flow.

### Declaration audit — 1 keep, 11 delete

The rule applied: **a default filter is legitimate when the hidden rows are
noise for the endpoint's primary consumer and the hidden state is managed
elsewhere. It is illegitimate when the list endpoint *is* the management
surface for the state being hidden.**

| Model | Endpoint | Declared | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account.Notification` | `/api/account/notification` | `{"is_unread": True}` | **KEEP** — the bell. Read rows are noise; `mark_read` is a by-pk POST action (`notification.py:69`), so nothing needs the read rows in the list. The reported case. |
| `account.User` | `/api/user` | `{"is_active": True}` | DELETE — `services/disable.py:99` flips `is_active` on disable; `/api/user` is where an admin finds a disabled user to reactivate. |
| `account.Group` | `/api/group` | `{"is_active": True}` | DELETE — same, via `on_action_disable`/`on_action_reactivate` (`group.py:600-631`). Also note `Group` has its own list path (`group.py:847-893`) that calls `on_rest_list` with an id-scoped queryset. |
| `account.GroupMember` | `/api/group/member` | `{"is_active": True}` | DELETE — flag never written `False` in `mojo/`; membership removal deletes the row. Unvalidated filter. |
| `account.Passkey` | `/api/account/passkeys` | `{"is_enabled": True}` | DELETE — `is_enabled` never written `False` in `mojo/`. If a disable flow lands later, a user must still see the disabled key to delete it. |
| `push.RegisteredDevice` | `/api/account/devices/push` | `{"is_active": True}` | DELETE — never written `False`; only read as a send-time gate (`services/push.py:69`). |
| `push.NotificationDelivery` | `/api/account/devices/push/deliveries` | `{"status": "sent"}` | DELETE — **actively wrong**: hides `delivered` and `failed` (finding 2 above). A delivery log exists to surface failures. |
| `push.PushConfig` | `/api/account/devices/push/config` | `{"is_active": True}` | DELETE — the runtime consumer already filters (`push/config.py:67,72`); the REST list is the admin surface for re-enabling a config. |
| `push.NotificationTemplate` | `/api/account/devices/push/templates` | `{"is_active": True}` | DELETE — same: the list is where you re-enable a template. |
| `phonehub.PhoneNumber` | `/api/phonehub/number` | `{"is_valid": True}` | DELETE — `is_valid` is written from the carrier lookup (`phone.py:131`); invalid numbers are the diagnostic value of the list. |
| `phonehub.PhoneConfig` | `/api/phonehub/config` | `{"is_active": True}` | DELETE — runtime consumer already filters (`config.py:116,121`); list is the admin surface. |
| `phonehub.SMS` | `/api/phonehub/sms` | `{}` | DELETE — empty, no-op, noise. |

Confirmed by Ian 2026-07-25, including the three dormant cases (`Passkey`,
`GroupMember`, `RegisteredDevice`): delete all eleven. Rationale — a filter
nobody has validated, sitting dormant until someone adds a disable flow and it
silently activates, is exactly the failure mode this item exists to fix.

All twelve models have live list endpoints (verified against `md.URL(...)`
handlers in `mojo/apps/account/rest/` and `mojo/apps/phonehub/rest/`), so none
of these is moot.

Net effect on shipped behavior: **only `/api/account/notification` changes**,
and it changes to what its own model already declared and what maestro already
requests explicitly. Every other endpoint returns exactly what it returns
today. That keeps the publish-to-PyPI blast radius at zero for web-mojo and
maestro while still fixing the framework.

`DM-048`'s "lists stay own-flag in v1" boundary is preserved by this outcome —
`Group`'s list keeps filtering nothing, which is what actually ships today.

### Implementation steps

**Step 1 — engine** (`mojo/models/rest.py`)

Add one classmethod next to the other list-filter helpers (after
`on_rest_list_filter`, ~line 1144):

```python
@classmethod
def on_rest_list_default_filters(cls, request, queryset, filters, excludes):
    """
    Apply RestMeta.LIST_DEFAULT_FILTERS as a baseline the request can override.

    The declared filters narrow the list by default (e.g. a notification
    list showing only unread rows). Precedence:

    - A request param naming the same BASE FIELD replaces that default
      entirely — ``?is_unread=false``, ``?is_unread__not=true``,
      ``?is_unread__in=true,false`` and ``?user.id=3`` all suppress a
      default keyed on that field. Suppression is per field, not per key,
      and covers exclusion filters as well as inclusion ones.
    - ``?_no_defaults=1`` drops every default for the request (admin
      surfaces that must see the full set).

    Defaults AND with whatever queryset the caller supplied, so the
    permission-scoped querysets from ``on_rest_handle_list`` keep their
    scoping.
    """
    defaults = cls.get_rest_meta_prop("LIST_DEFAULT_FILTERS", None)
    if not defaults:
        return queryset
    if request.DATA.get_typed("_no_defaults", False, bool):
        return queryset
    named = {key.split("__")[0] for key in filters}
    named.update(key.split("__")[0] for key in excludes)
    applied = {k: v for k, v in defaults.items() if k.split("__")[0] not in named}
    if applied:
        queryset = queryset.filter(**applied)
    return queryset
```

Wire it into `on_rest_list_filter` (`:1138-1143`), which already has the
parsed dicts in hand:

```python
filters, excludes = cls.build_rest_filters(request, request.QUERY_PARAMS)
queryset = cls.on_rest_list_default_filters(request, queryset, filters, excludes)
queryset = cls.on_rest_list_search(request, queryset)
queryset = queryset.filter(**filters)
if excludes:
    queryset = queryset.exclude(**excludes)
return queryset
```

Also extend the `on_rest_list_filter` docstring with a one-line pointer to the
new baseline behavior.

**Step 2 — declaration audit.** Delete the `LIST_DEFAULT_FILTERS` line(s) from
the eleven models in the DELETE column above. Keep `notification.py:51`. The
commit message carries the one-line rationale per model (the table's Verdict
column).

**Step 3 — tests** (`tests/test_models/list_default_filters.py`, new).

**Step 4 — docs.**

**Step 5 — `CHANGELOG.md`** entry under the rolling block.

### Design decisions

- **Why inside `on_rest_list_filter`, not `on_rest_list`.** The suppression set
  must come from the *parsed* filter keys, and those only exist inside
  `on_rest_list_filter`. Putting the call anywhere else means re-parsing
  `QUERY_PARAMS` and re-implementing every skip rule in `build_rest_filters`
  (reserved bare params, `_` prefix, `.`→`__`, "is this even a field") —
  duplication that would drift. Nothing overrides `on_rest_list_filter`
  anywhere in `mojo/` (verified), so there is no lost-defaults risk from
  subclassing today. The aggregation branch (`_mode`, `on_rest_list:828-831`)
  reads the queryset *after* `on_rest_list_filter` returns, so it inherits
  defaults for free — `rest_aggregation.py`'s module docstring already promises
  "permissions, group scope, field filters, and date-range filters" are
  pre-applied; defaults join that list.

- **Why field-level, not key-level, suppression.** Key-level matching is the
  trap this item exists to avoid: `?is_unread__not=true` parses into
  `excludes`, so a key-level check would leave the `is_unread=True` default in
  `filters` and AND the two into a guaranteed-empty result. Comparing
  `key.split("__")[0]` on both dicts is the whole fix, and it also handles a
  default that itself carries a lookup (`{"status__in": [...]}`).

- **Why `?_no_defaults=1` and not `?field=all`.** Confirmed with Ian. A magic
  `"all"` value collides with any field that can legitimately hold the string.
  The `_` prefix namespace is already reserved and already skipped by
  `build_rest_filters:1032`, and `docs/django_developer/core/mojo_model.md:192`
  already documents it as reserved for "the aggregation surface (or other
  framework features)" — so this needs no new reserved-key plumbing and no
  contract change.

- **Why `get_typed(..., bool)` for the off-switch.** `request.DATA.get("_no_defaults")`
  returns the *string* `"0"` for `?_no_defaults=0`, which is truthy — a naive
  check would invert the caller's intent. `objict.get_typed` coerces via the
  explicit allow-list `[1, '1', 'y', 'Y', 'on', 'T', 't', 'True', 'true']`, and
  returns `False` when the key is absent. Same helper `on_rest_list_response`
  already uses for `size`/`start`.

- **Why the empty-defaults short-circuit comes first.** Almost every model in
  the framework has no declaration; `get_rest_meta_prop` is a plain `getattr`
  (no caching), so the cheap `if not defaults: return queryset` keeps the hot
  path free of set-building and `request.DATA` access. This also makes the
  change a provable no-op for every model except `Notification`.

- **What is deliberately left alone.** The assistant's `query_model` tool
  (`mojo/apps/assistant/services/tools/models.py:544-590`) builds its own
  queryset and calls `on_rest_list_search` directly — it never enters
  `on_rest_list`, so it keeps returning unfiltered rows. Bringing it under
  default filters is a separate behavioral decision about the assistant's data
  access, not part of this fix.

### Edge cases and error handling

- **Default keyed on a field the request also sorts by** (`?sort=-is_unread`) —
  `sort` is a reserved bare param that never reaches `filters`, so the default
  still applies. Correct: sorting is not filtering.
- **Default keyed on a field the model no longer has** — `queryset.filter()`
  raises `FieldError`, a 500. Acceptable and desirable: it is a developer error
  in the declaration, surfaced loudly at first request rather than silently
  ignored (which is precisely the failure mode being fixed). Not worth a guard.
- **`?group=` deletion** (`on_rest_list:819-820`) happens before
  `on_rest_list_filter`, so a default keyed on `group` would apply even when
  the caller passed `?group=`. No declaration does this after the audit; noted
  so a future declaration doesn't trip on it.
- **Empty dict `{}`** — falsy, short-circuits identically to absent. (The
  `phonehub/sms.py` case, deleted anyway.)
- **Date defaults** — a declared `{"created__gte": ...}` would suppress on base
  name `created`, so `?created=2026-04` (which expands to
  `created__gte`/`created__lte`) correctly replaces it. No declaration does
  this today; the mechanism handles it.
- **Synthetic requests without `DATA`** — every caller of `on_rest_list` in
  `mojo/` supplies `request.DATA` (`on_rest_list:828` already dereferences it
  unconditionally), so no defensive `getattr` is warranted.

### Testing plan

New module `tests/test_models/list_default_filters.py`, following the
two-surface structure of `tests/test_models/list_stats.py` (direct calls for
mechanics, `opts.client` for the wire contract).

Host model: `account.Notification` — it is the one surviving declaration, its
`VIEW_PERMS = ["owner"]` routes the list through the owner-scoped branch at
`rest.py:593`, so the perm-scoped composition criterion is proven for free
rather than staged. No monkeypatching of `RestMeta` anywhere: per
`.claude/rules/testing.md`, `opts.client` hits a **separate server process**
where in-process patches have no effect, and the direct-call tests use the
model's real declaration.

Setup (`@th.django_unit_setup()`): create `ldf_user` and `ldf_other` with
verified email + password; **delete their existing notifications first**
(long-lived DB); then create for `ldf_user` one unread and one read
notification (`Notification.send(..., push=False, ws=False)` then flip
`is_unread=False` on one), plus one unread for `ldf_other`.

Direct-call tests (synthetic request built like `date_filtering.py:24-37`,
asserting on the queryset returned by
`Notification.on_rest_list_default_filters(...)`):

1. baseline applied — no params → only the unread row
2. same-field param replaces — `filters={"is_unread": False}` → only the read row
3. exclusion form replaces — `excludes={"is_unread": True}` → default dropped
4. `__in` form replaces — `filters={"is_unread__in": [True, False]}` → both
5. dotted/relation key on a *different* field does **not** suppress — e.g. a
   `user` filter leaves the `is_unread` default in force
6. off-switch — `_no_defaults=1` → both rows
7. off-switch is parsed as a bool — `_no_defaults=0` → only unread (guards the
   `"0"`-is-truthy trap)
8. no-declaration model is untouched — same call on a model without the prop
   (e.g. `shortlink.ShortLink`) returns the queryset unchanged

End-to-end through `opts.client` (`/api/account/notification`):

9. **the regression** — logged in as `ldf_user`, bare `GET` returns only the
   unread row. Fails on current code (returns both), passes on the fix.
10. `?is_unread=false` returns only the read row
11. `?_no_defaults=1` returns both
12. owner scoping still holds — `ldf_other`'s notification never appears in any
    of the above
13. `?_mode=count` matches the default-filtered list count (aggregation
    inherits defaults)

Run: `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_models.list_default_filters`, then the full
default suite. Baseline first per `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md` — capture
`var/test_failures.json` **before** the first edit and record it under
`## Notes` on the board item.

Every `assert` carries a descriptive failure message (`.claude/rules/testing.md`).

### Build routing

Default — inline, session model.
